---
title: "4. Linking area data"
format: html
---

For each patient's first Medical Evidence form, this script adds what is known about the place they lived: the number of dialysis facilities in their ZIP code and HSA on the day dialysis started, census (ACS) data for the ZIP code, the HSA's population and Dartmouth Atlas benchmarks, whether the area is rural or urban, and the cause of kidney failure. It then calculates the study's exposure, dialysis facilities per 100,000 HSA residents. No patients are removed at this step; those with missing area data are excluded later, as steps in the [cohort flowchart](create_cohort.qmd).

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/link_area_data.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/link_area_data.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/functions.R)
-   [`R/download_public_data.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/download_public_data.R)
-   [`R/prepare_patients.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/prepare_patients.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false

```

## Cause of kidney failure mapping

The reviewed mapping, written by [Classifying codes](classify_esrd_causes.qmd), must exist and give every code one of the six categories; otherwise the run stops with instructions. Only `code` and `final_category` are read.

```{r}
#| label: read-cause-mapping
#| eval: false
```

A first form whose cause code is blank, or is not in the mapping, counts as Other, as in the original code. A blank cause is expected; a code that is filled in but missing from the mapping is not, and many of them would suggest that the codes are written differently in the Medical Evidence file and in the code list (case, spaces, leading zeros). That would move real causes into Other without any error, so the script warns with the share of first forms affected.

```{r}
#| label: check-unmapped-causes
#| eval: false
```

## Facility counts on the dialysis date

This is the step the original code spent most of its length on: it expanded every CMS file to one row per ZIP code per day, over 15 years, to look up counts by date. `usRds::add_dialysis_facility_counts()` instead finds the CMS release current on each patient's date of dialysis start and counts facilities in the ZIP code and in its HSA, with an interval join that cannot multiply rows. It also fixes two errors in the original counts (see [Differences](differences.qmd)).

```{r}
#| label: attach-facility-counts
#| eval: false
```

## ACS, HSA and other area data

Each ZIP code is mapped to its ZCTA with the crosswalk for the year dialysis started, and ACS data are joined by ZCTA; the HSA and its population are matched by ZIP code and the same year, so area data and facility counts describe the same year. The original code used the year of the form for area data and silently dropped patients whose two years differed. Every join states its expected relationship, so an unexpected duplicate stops the run.

```{r}
#| label: attach-area-data
#| eval: false
```

## Facility density

Facilities per 100,000 HSA residents, plus the availability flags the flowchart filters on. A patient has an HSA only if the HSA's density is a finite number: an HSA whose population is zero would give an infinite density, so it counts as having no HSA.
